body:
## Change and mathematical scope

This PR adds an opt-in verification package under
`research/joint-frame-modular-screen/` for the historical
`scripts/audit_joint_frames.py` certificate.

It uses exact elimination modulo 101 to certify full rational rank.
Rank-deficient modular reductions and denominators divisible by 101
fall back to the unchanged original rational elimination routine.
No approximate rank decision is used.

The supplied benchmark records median complete-certificate wall time
of 1.952577 s for the reference engine and 1.701918 s for the screened
engine: 12.8% lower across seven alternating fresh-process A/B pairs.
All fourteen timed certificates are byte-identical. One pair was slower;
the timing result is specific to the recorded environment.

This is a tooling improvement. No new construction, improved kappa,
or practical integer-multiplication speedup is claimed.

## Provenance

- Exact investigation base: `66849e1475c930fd7732b1a0067ffee7e1e95f60`
- Assignment track: verification engineering
- OS-random assignment seed: 85
- `SOURCE.json` pins 36 predecessor inputs with SHA-256 and Git-blob IDs.
- `CLAIM.json` records the local claim and overlap review.
- `NOTICE.md` credits predecessor and related concurrent work.

The investigation base above is the base recorded during preparation,
not a claim that it is the current tip of the PR's destination branch.

## Validation

The supplied preparation record reports:

- All 2,644 actual uncached rank calls individually agree with the
  original routine: 752 modular certificates and 1,892 exact fallbacks.
- 12 focused test groups, including an independent determinant/minor
  oracle over 530 binary matrices and 240 seed-85 rational matrices.
- Four deliberately incorrect kernels detected by counterexamples.
- All eight unchanged historical tests pass with both engines.
- All fourteen timed complete certificates match exactly.
- Source-drift controls and rejection of disabled assertions.
- Successful `make selected-record-check` and staged whitespace checks.

Reproduce from the repository root with Python 3.11+ on Linux or macOS,
using a fresh output path:

```sh
python3 -I -B research/joint-frame-modular-screen/verify.py --pairs 7 --output /tmp/joint-frame-rank-result.json
```

Expected final marker:

```text
PASS_JOINT_FRAME_MODULAR_SCREEN
```

These are recorded preparation results; no independent human rerun
or verification on the newly uploaded branch is asserted.

## Scope and limitations

Only the research package is intended to be added. Existing scripts,
default verification commands, the selected frontier, and `upstream/`
are intended to remain unchanged.

`PROOF.md` provides the algebraic equivalence argument for the fast path.
Finite tests and certificate replays are not a formal proof of the full
multiplication theorem.

Full repository `make verify`, selected cold reconstruction, Lean builds,
and hosted CI were not run during preparation and are not claimed.

The recorded overlap review was performed at
2026-10-13T05:15:10.714617Z and does not cover subsequent contributions.

## Attribution and AI assistance

Prepared at Martin Rivera's request with substantial OpenAI Codex
assistance, as disclosed in `NOTICE.md`. The assistant implemented the
optimization, wrote the argument and tests, recorded the measurements,
and prepared the handoff.

No independent human review or official OpenAI endorsement is claimed.
The contribution is under Apache-2.0.
title: Tooling: exact modular rank fast path for historical joint-frame verification
